# The pipeline

> **Answer first.** What every `cargo xtask` command does, in order, what it writes and what it starts — and, for any generated file, which commands write it.
>
> **Kind:** reference · **For:** developers, maintainers

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask pipeline` from docs/manual.toml. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every `cargo xtask` command: what it does, in order, what it writes and what it starts. `cargo xtask explain <command>` prints one of these; `--dry-run` on any command prints it and runs nothing; `cargo xtask why <path>` names the commands that write a file. Each run is recorded in `target/xtask-trace.log`.

## docs

`cargo xtask docs [<node>]`

Generate each row's files from its sheet. Never reads another row.

1. load the tree
2. refuse a published node with an unanswered field (after writing the rest)
3. write each node's generated files, only where they changed
4. write the kernel's method files, removing any no node has
5. write docs/PSEUDOCODE.md when no node is named

## assemble

`cargo xtask assemble`

The assembly validations, then the index and the page fragments the browser serves.

1. load the tree
2. run the assembly validations; stop on a refusal unless --force
3. write the index and each node's page fragment

## gate

`cargo xtask gate [<node>]`

The checks, in order. The one that must pass.

1. load the tree
2. every check on every node, or on the one named
3. the whole-tree checks
4. stop with the count of failures

## status

`cargo xtask status`

Counts by state and subsystem, and what is holding the tree back.

1. load the tree
2. count by state and subsystem

## active

`cargo xtask active [<subsystem>]`

Which rows answer, and for each that does not, whether its own derivation or a row it reads is missing.

1. load the tree
2. for each row: answers, or what it is missing

## reach

`cargo xtask reach [<subsystem>]`

Where each answer goes, and which reach no customer target.

1. load the tree
2. follow each answer to the KPI closures

## gap

`cargo xtask gap`

What every sheet promised and nothing yet covers.

1. load the tree
2. list every promise nothing covers

## graph

`cargo xtask graph`

The three graphs, their sizes, and the check that every crate depends inward.

1. load the tree
2. size the three graphs
3. check crate directions from each Cargo.toml

## new

`cargo xtask new <id> --like <sibling>`

Start a row from a sibling's shape, with everything that must be re-decided blanked.

1. load the tree
2. clone the sibling's sheet, blanking what must be decided again
3. write the new node's folder, node.toml and fixtures.toml
4. move the order of every later node up by one

## declare

`cargo xtask declare <node>`

The questions a sheet still has open, and what goes wrong without each.

1. load the tree
2. print the completion questions, in order

## fill

`cargo xtask fill <node> --hole <n> --body <file|-> [--by <who> --model <model>]`

Put the Rust for one numbered slot into a row's generated model. `--by` and `--model` record who wrote it, and with what.

1. refuse a body with markers, faults or platform maths
2. check who wrote it
3. splice it into model.rs and read it back
4. record the fill in fills.toml with --by and --model

## differential

`cargo xtask differential <node>`

Compare two recorded bodies for the same slot, written by different model families.

1. for each recorded body of the hole: put it in model.rs and run the node's tests
2. put model.rs back

## form

`cargo xtask form <node>|--new [--example] [--out <file.html>]`

A node's form: one self-contained HTML file that explains itself, asks every question the sheet answers, and saves a filled copy. `--new` is the form for a node the design does not have yet. Filled anywhere, by anyone. --example fills orbit_velocity's form with the worked example, only for the pipeline's end-to-end test of the method path; nothing it produces is committed.

1. load the tree
2. write the node's form — to --out, or to the screen

## intake

`cargo xtask intake <file.html> [--apply [--partial]]`

The checker: what a filled node form would change, field by field, and every interface it declares — conflicts and refusals named. `--apply` writes (building a new node in its place), regenerates and gates as one edit, or puts everything back.

1. read the filled form and plan the change, field by field
2. stop here without --apply
3. with --apply: write node.toml (a new node: build its folder first)
4. regenerate, gate; on a refusal put every file back
5. a new node: rewrite CODEOWNERS

## publish

`cargo xtask publish <node>`

Move a filled, seeded row to published, so its code is generated and its slots can be written. Refuses, naming every reason, while it is not ready.

1. load the tree
2. refuse, naming every reason, while it is not ready
3. set state = published in node.toml
4. generate its files for the first time and gate the whole tree; on a refusal put it back

## guides

`cargo xtask guides`

Renders the three role guides — docs/roles/user.html, maintainer.html and developer.html — from this manual. Never edited by hand: the pipeline regenerates them and fails when a committed one differs.

1. read docs/manual.toml
2. render each role guide

## method

`cargo xtask method <node>`

Checks a node's method in the method language and runs each of its author's test cases through it: what their code gave, what the method gives, and whether the set is complete — at least three answers and one refusal. The same check the node form runs as the author types, and the gate refuses on.

1. load the tree
2. check the node's method and run its cases

## method-wasm

`cargo xtask method-wasm [--check]`

Builds the method checker every node form carries — vleo_sheet::method compiled to WebAssembly — into web/method.wasm.gz with the fingerprint of its sources; --check only says whether the committed file is current.

1. with --check: only say whether web/method.wasm.gz is current
2. build the checker for wasm32
3. gzip it and write the stamp

## rerun

`cargo xtask rerun <node>|--all [--require]`

Runs each author's own code again on the cases recorded from it and says whether it still gives them: Python directly, MATLAB and Octave through Octave where it is installed. Code in any other language is kept and read, not rerun, and it says so; `--require` fails instead, for a pipeline that installed the runners.

1. write the author's code and a harness in a temporary folder
2. run it: python3, or octave
3. compare with the cases; remove the folder

## build-node

`cargo xtask build-node <node>`

Builds a node from its method, stage by stage, stopping at the first that fails: the method on its author's cases; the translation into the kernel; the node's tests — the author's cases and the translation against the method; the author's code rerun; a mutation the tests must catch; and only then the node in the tree.

1. M: the method on its cases
2. G1: generate the node's files
3. T1+T2: its tests
4. T3: the author's code run again
5. T4: a mutation its tests must catch
6. I1: gate the node and the tree

## migration

`cargo xtask migration [--owner <o>] [--subsystem <s>] [--forms <dir>]`

Says which computed rows still need a method, by owner, and with --forms writes each one's node form into <dir>/<owner>/ ready to send. It writes no method: each comes from the node's owner, on the node's form, through take like any other change.

1. load the tree
2. list the computed rows still without a method, by owner
3. with --forms: write each one's form

## take

`cargo xtask take <form.html> --for <author> [--again] [--no-push] [--no-test]`

Takes a filled node form in: checks it, and if it cannot be taken writes `<form>.returned.txt` to send back and changes nothing; otherwise puts it on its own branch `form/<author>/<node>` from a fresh main, applies it, regenerates, gates, tests, commits naming the author and pushes. The push builds the author's preview.

1. check the form; if it cannot be taken, write <form>.returned.txt and stop
2. refuse an unclean working tree
3. branch form/<author>/<node> from a fresh origin/main
4. apply it (intake --apply)
5. regenerate CODEOWNERS, VARIABLES, the de-risking narrative
6. gate
7. build-node and cargo test, unless --no-test
8. commit naming the author; push unless --no-push

## preview

`cargo xtask preview`

Where the current form branch's preview build is, and what to do with it. Every push to a form branch builds one by itself.

1. read the branch and its remote
2. say where its preview build is

## approve

`cargo xtask approve <approval.toml> [--no-push]`

Records the author's approval of a preview — the file the preview saves when they press Approve. Refused unless it is for the build of exactly what is on the branch now. `--verify <branch>` is the same check, as the pipeline runs it.

1. with --verify: only check the approval against the branch
2. refuse an unclean working tree
3. check the approval is for the build of what is here
4. copy it into approvals/
5. commit; push unless --no-push

## queue

`cargo xtask queue`

Every form branch and where it stands: not pushed, waiting for the author's approval, approved and ready to merge, or merged.

1. fetch the remote
2. list every form branch and where it stands

## ship

`cargo xtask ship <version> [--no-push] [--no-test]`

Cuts a release from main on its own branch `release/<version>`: the de-risking narrative, the version stamp, regeneration, the gate and the tests, one commit, pushed — and prints the tag commands for after the merge.

1. refuse unless on a clean main equal to origin/main
2. branch release/<version>
3. write the de-risking narrative
4. release <version>: stamp, set the version, regenerate
5. regenerate VARIABLES, CODEOWNERS, the guides, the lockfiles
6. gate; cargo test unless --no-test
7. commit; push unless --no-push

## kit

`cargo xtask kit [--bin <dir>] [--out <dir>] [--files-only]`

The tool as a team member gets it: the two release-built programs beside exactly the files they read, with START_HERE.md and VERSION (and start.sh off Windows, where the daemon ships as Start VLEO.exe), in dist/vleo-<version>/. Zip it and share it; see docs/SHARING.md. --files-only leaves the programs out: the files the Python package carries.

1. empty --out (default dist/vleo-<version>/)
2. copy the web face, the tree, its pages and the reference data
3. copy the programs; on Windows the daemon becomes Start VLEO.exe
4. write START_HERE.md, VERSION and start.sh

## derisk

`cargo xtask derisk`

Write the de-risking narrative — docs/DERISK_NARRATIVE.md and docs/derisking.csv — from every node's `[[version]]` record and the risk register. Generated, never edited.

1. load the tree
2. write every recorded change and every registered risk

## release

`cargo xtask release <version> [--check]`

Stamp every node version still marked `next` with this release, set the workspace version and regenerate. `--check` refuses while anything is unstamped — the release pipeline runs it.

1. with --check: only refuse while anything is unstamped or newer
2. refuse a node version that names a later release
3. stamp every `next` node version with this release
4. set the workspace version; cargo refreshes the lockfiles
5. regenerate: docs, then derisk

## confirm

`cargo xtask confirm <node> --by "<name>"`

Put a person's name against a relation, after printing it and its source. `confirm --list` shows the ones with no name yet.

1. with --list: only list the relations nobody has confirmed
2. print the relation and its source
3. write confirmed_by into node.toml, and read it back

## ready

`cargo xtask ready [<node>]`

Whether a person should be asked to look yet.

1. the gate
2. the gap pass
3. what the node's criticality demands

## codeowners

`cargo xtask codeowners`

Regenerate CODEOWNERS from the layer files.

1. load the tree
2. write CODEOWNERS from the owners

## bundle

`cargo xtask bundle publish <dir>`

`bundle verify` re-checks every published set's hashes. `bundle publish` publishes a new one, permanently.

1. verify: re-check every hash in bundles/
2. publish <dir>: hash every payload and write it into the manifest

## mutate

`cargo xtask mutate [<node>]`

Perturb a row's answer and require its own tests to notice. Puts the row back.

1. for each published node: perturb its answer in model.rs
2. require its own tests to fail
3. put model.rs back

## setup

`cargo xtask setup`

Point git at the project's hooks. Once per checkout.

1. check the hooks in tools/githooks are executable
2. set git's core.hooksPath to tools/githooks

## explain

`cargo xtask explain [<command>]`

What a command does, in order, what it writes and what it starts — from this manual. `--dry-run` on any command prints the same and runs nothing.

1. read docs/manual.toml
2. print the command's steps, writes and the programs it starts

## why

`cargo xtask why <path>`

Which commands write a file — so whether it is generated, and what to change instead of it.

1. read docs/manual.toml
2. match the path against every command's writes

## pipeline

`cargo xtask pipeline [--check]`

Write docs/PIPELINE.md: every command's steps, and every generated file with the commands that write it. `--check` only says whether it is current.

1. read docs/manual.toml
2. with --check: only say whether docs/PIPELINE.md is current
3. write docs/PIPELINE.md

## variables

`cargo xtask variables`

Write docs/VARIABLES.md — every variable, its unit, its range and why.

1. load the tree
2. write every variable, its unit, range and readers
